items.title: Jillean Williams interviewed by Milt Fillius and Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 20, 1995
items.q: he went out for a while with Sweets in a group, Jerome Richardson and Sweets, and a wonderful group of musicians

ctx.x: But Joe went on to become a great single, and his own group of course. Were there tough times when he broke loose on his own?

Not professionally tough times, no. I fact I don’t know any tough times. Basie saw him off. Basie came up and introduced him on his first single job, which was in Boston, and he went out for a while with Sweets in a group, Jerome Richardson and Sweets, and a wonderful group of musicians. And he always seemed to have work, we never had any bad years that I can remember. So I think he’s done real well. And actually he seems to be getting better and better. Everybody thinks his voice is still wonderful.
Well I told you that I think so. I think he and Tony Bennett are the only two musicians of the older ranks whose voices are better now then they were when they were younger. Maybe Mel Torme, maybe.
